title: Generating multiple stage-matched C. elegans hybrids and parental strains simultaneously
author: Avery Davis Bell
materials: Re-use 1mL of buffer on several plates
Flash freeze tubes in liquid nitrogen

Set up for RNA extraction. Full details on reagents and equipment are found in the appropriate sections; this step describes set up for this specific experiment. Plan to extract RNA in batches of no more than 18 samples/batch, with one sample per strain in each batch (likely 1 or 3 batches) Equipment: Heat block set to 37°C Procure dewer of liquid nitrogen for freeze-thawing Centrifuge at (or set to) room temperature Centrifuge at (or set to) 4°C Reagents: TRIzol (fume hood!) Chloroform (fume hood!) Freshly prepared 70% ethanol Qiagen RNeasy buffer RW1 Qiagen RNeasy buffer RPE (with ethanol added as directed by the kit) RNAse-free water Sets of tubes to label: 1.5mL tubes for aqueous phase after TRIzol-chloroform spin RNeasy spin columns 1.5mL tubes for eluted RNA collection Clean with RNAse away: Gloves Fume hood Outside of tip boxes, reagents to be used Freeze thaw area Centrifuge area
Freeze by submerging tube in liquid nitrogen

steps.title: Grow parental worm cultures
steps.instruction: Follow standard C. elegans culture (Stiernagle 2006). Grow all strains at ≤18 °C if they have mortal germline phenotypes. Maintain ~15 plates of the common reference strain and enough plates of each wild strain for later crosses.

steps.title: Establish male‑heavy cultures
steps.instruction: For each wild strain to be crossed to the reference, start cultures enriched for males and propagate (e.g., by chunking) until plates contain many visible males.

steps.title: Set up initial mating plates
steps.instruction: On each mating plate place 20–30 hermaphrodites of the reference strain and as many males from the wild strain as available (minimum 3, maximum 45). Repeat plate setup until a high male density is visible; then propagate those male cultures normally.

steps.title: Bleach‑synchronize parental strains (Day 1)
steps.instruction: Bleach‑sync all parental strains and re‑plate embryos onto fresh NGM/Agarose plates. Use only non‑starved plates. For each wild strain wash 2–3 plates and for the reference strain wash 10–15 plates into a 15 mL conical tube with water.

substeps.instruction: Wash plates into tube, centrifuge 2000 rpm 2 min, discard supernatant without disturbing pellet.
Add 7 mL water + 3 mL 2:1 bleach:NaOH (5 M) (total 10 mL). Gently shake 5–7 min; monitor under stereoscope. When carcasses are largely dissolved (≈7 min) centrifuge as before.
Remove bleaching solution, resuspend pellet in 13 mL water, shake vigorously, centrifuge again.
Repeat the water wash once more and discard supernatant.
Resuspend embryos in water and distribute onto NGM/Agarose plates as needed.

steps.title: Incubate plates at varied temperatures
steps.instruction: Maintain several growing plates per strain. Grow reference‑strain plates at 18 °C, 19 °C, 20 °C, and room temperature; grow wild‑strain plates at a subset of these temperatures to ensure appropriate developmental stages for later mating.

steps.title: Set up mating plates (Day 3)
steps.instruction: For each wild strain, prepare five mating plates: add 60 L4 reference‑strain hermaphrodites to each plate, screen to confirm no males, then add 40 L4 wild‑strain males. Also prepare three plates per strain with 80 L4 wild‑strain hermaphrodites (selfed offspring will serve as parental controls). Incubate plates for 48 h at 20 °C to allow mating.

steps.title: Harvest worms and embryos (Day 5)
steps.instruction: Wash all worms, bacteria, and embryos from each cross (or parental selfing) into a single 15 mL conical tube, collecting all embryos. Rinse each plate twice with water, then gently swipe a glass pipette tip across the plate surface while expelling water (plate angled) to dislodge embryos without agar. Repeat until the lawn is visually cleared. Add water to each tube to a total volume of 14 mL, spin 2000 rpm 2 min, and vacuum‑remove most liquid without disturbing the pellet.

steps.title: Bleach embryos for L1 synchronization
steps.instruction: Resuspend each pellet to 3.5 mL water, add 1.5 mL 2:1 bleach:NaOH solution, start timer, shake every 30 s, and monitor. When adult carcasses fully dissolve (≈7 min), add water to bring volume to 14 mL, spin 2000 rpm 2 min, and vacuum‑aspirate bleaching solution close to the pellet. Resuspend to 10 mL water, spin 2000 rpm 2 min, vacuum‑aspirate to a final volume of 1.5 mL. Resuspend pellet in 15 mL water containing 0.25 % Tween‑20, spin 2000 rpm 2 min (orient tubes so interior striations are not on the inside). Vacuum‑aspirate as close to the pellet as possible, then resuspend with water to wash out detergent. Spin again 2000 rpm 2 min, vacuum‑aspirate, and finally resuspend embryo pellet in 10 mL M9 buffer. Keep tubes gently rocking at room temperature; embryos will develop to L1 and arrest.

steps.title: Add Tween‑20 to L1 suspension
steps.instruction: ≈30 h after embryos are in M9, add Tween‑20 to a final concentration of 0.25 %: either add 25 µL pure Tween‑20 directly to each tube, or add 200 µL of a 1:250 diluted Tween‑20 (500 µL Tween‑20 mixed with 4 mL water) to each tube. Spin 2000 rpm 2 min, vacuum‑aspirate leaving <0.5 mL liquid; the loose L1 pellet should remain undisturbed.

steps.title: Count L1s and seed plates
steps.instruction: Place a 10 µL droplet of the mixed worm suspension onto an empty 6 cm plate, count L1s by eye under a microscope, and record the number. Calculate the volume containing 400 worms and add that volume to three or more 6 cm large‑lawn plates per strain (split into multiple spots if needed). Allow droplets to absorb with lids off for a few minutes.

steps.title: Remove males from F1 plates
steps.instruction: On Day 8, inspect at least three plates per strain and manually pick off visible males (F1s are ~50 % male, appearing ~32–36 h after un‑sync). Parental plates require only occasional checks for spontaneous males.

steps.title: Harvest adults for RNA (Day 9)
steps.instruction: Identify strains where most hermaphrodites are gravid (~55–60 h after un‑sync at 20 °C). Remove any stray males and group developmentally similar strains. For each strain, rinse all plates twice with M9 into a 15 mL tube, ensuring only adult worms are collected (avoid bacteria and embryos). Spin 2000 rpm 2 min, vacuum‑remove buffer close to the pellet, resuspend in 13 mL M9, spin again 2000 rpm 2 min, and vacuum‑remove buffer.

steps.title: Add TRIzol and freeze
steps.instruction: Add TRIzol to each tube to a final volume of ~1.5 mL (≈1.2 mL TRIzol). Aliquot the worm‑TRIzol mixture into three 1.5 mL microcentrifuge tubes (~500 µL per tube). Store at –80 °C until RNA extraction.

steps.title: Perform freeze‑thaw cycles
steps.instruction: Vortex each frozen tube for 2 min, then thaw at room temperature; repeat for a total of six freeze‑thaw cycles, spinning down between cycles.

steps.title: Phase separation with chloroform
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL fresh TRIzol to each tube, incubate 5 min at room temperature, add 140 µL chloroform, shake at 1450 rpm for 1 min, incubate 2 min at room temperature, then centrifuge 12,000 g 15 min at 4 °C. Transfer the aqueous phase to a new tube.

steps.title: Purify RNA on RNeasy columns
steps.instruction: Add an equal volume of 70 % ethanol to the aqueous phase, mix, and load onto a Qiagen RNeasy spin column. Spin 30 s at max speed, discard flow‑through. Add remaining sample with 700 µL RW1 buffer, spin 30 s, discard flow‑through. Add 500 µL RPE buffer, spin 30 s, discard flow‑through; repeat the RPE wash once more. Spin column at max speed for 2 min to remove residual buffer, transfer column to a new labeled tube, add 50 µL RNase‑free water, incubate 1 min at room temperature, spin 1 min, and collect eluate. Keep RNA on ice, quantify, and store at –80 °C.
